source.title: Accelerating Asynchronous Stochastic Gradient Descent for Neural Machine Translation
source.authors: Nikolay Bogoychev; Marcin Junczys-dowmunt; K. Heafield; Alham Fikri Aji

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Reports batch-size and optimizer effects on translation validation cross-entropy and BLEU, extending batch-size findings to neural machine translation. It does not directly measure the train–test error gap.
record.gate_note: The paper reports translation performance for larger effective batches and modified training recipes. Speed-only results and cited findings from other work are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: The study directly varies effective batch size and training adjustments in neural machine translation, extending V5 to a new workload. Final-score comparisons use validation-based stopping rather than fixed epoch budgets, but Figure 3 also compares validation cross-entropy epoch for epoch.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors conclude that larger effective batches can accelerate asynchronous NMT training while preserving convergence through momentum tuning and warmup/cooldown. They report negligible BLEU loss for the shallow system and practically unchanged BLEU with better validation CE for the deep system.
record.recipe_differences: Studies asynchronous NMT training with delayed gradient updates, local optimizers, warmup, and momentum tuning; it does not use the fixed-epoch image-classification or language-model comparisons described in V5.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch factor τ, warmup strategy, local optimizers, and momentum tuning/cooldown change convergence and reported translation performance.
record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: No direct train–test error gap is measured; the Romanian-English systems train until validation cross-entropy stalls rather than for a fixed number of epochs. The deep-model asynchronous baseline could not achieve competitive BLEU without delayed updates, so Table 3 does not isolate the batch-size effect. No uncertainty estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: No results omitted. Speed-only WPS and training-time measurements in Tables 1–3 are excluded because they do not measure held-out performance or the train–test gap.

untested.parts: Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizers under limited or broader tuning; synchronization comparisons do not test this.

The unadapted large-batch penalty under a controlled fixed epoch budget is not established by the endpoint rows. Image classifiers and standalone language models are not studied. Batch effects are entangled with asynchronous gradient staleness.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.

missing.what: Epoch-matched validation CE for the deep English-German model: the adapted fourfold-batch system has lower CE epoch for epoch. This bears directly on V5's budget condition and is not represented by endpoint R16.

Larger delay factors could not maintain convergence for the shallow Romanian-English model, although they worked for the deep model. The text reports this qualitatively without scores or a precise failing delay factor.
The adapted shallow system initially has worse epoch-matched convergence but catches up later, showing that apparent recovery depends on training duration.

record.verdict_notes: States describe the large-batch performance penalty: absent or reversed states under adapted recipes can support V5's explicit mitigation clause. A train–test gap is not required to assess V5's held-out-performance claim. No statistical uncertainty is reported, and the study is not an original source for any version.

versions.untested_parts: Network width beyond the interpolation threshold.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer generalization under tuning.
Fixed epoch budgets, image classifiers, language models, and direct train–test gap measurements; the paper studies translation systems and trains to a validation-stall criterion.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other measures of the generalization gap.

relationships.condition: Shallow Romanian-English translation with doubled effective batches and no compensating warmup or momentum changes; validation-based stopping
relationships.reason: R3–R4 show BLEU falling 35.56→34.82 and validation CE rising 50.90→51.68 despite an additional epoch; this supports the batch-penalty component in this new setting, without establishing its fixed-budget formulation.
relationships.display_finding: Doubling the effective batch size reduced BLEU from 35.56 to 34.82 and increased validation cross-entropy despite an additional epoch, without establishing a fixed-epoch penalty.
